text: In March 1985, Chandmal Chopra petitioned the Calcutta High Court to ban the Quran, alleging that it incited violence and promoted enmity among different sections; the High Court disallowed the petition on May 17, 1985. In 2013 a district court in Novorossiysk ruled that a translation of the Quran by Elmir Kuliyev was extremist and should be included on the federal list of banned literature, and the Krasnodar regional court later overturned that ruling. Malaysia's Home Ministry prohibited 10 translations of the Quran in Malay, English, Chinese and Korean in 2017; its chief secretary, Alwi Ibrahim, said they had been printed without the original verses in Arabic.
meta_description: Quran: Calcutta High Court disallowed a 1985 petition to ban it; a Russian court's 2013 ruling on a translation was overturned; Malaysia prohibited 10 translations.
changes: Years attached to the Russian and Malaysian events from the ban rows; chronological order; the petition is described as a petition, not a ban.
